title: ConfigureAwait(false)
sub: Skipping the context, and when that's dangerous
cards/0/title: Don't go back to the context
cards/0/body:
ConfigureAwait(false) says: "the continuation doesn't have to run in the captured context". It goes to the pool instead.

That's right for library code that doesn't need the UI thread: fewer switches, and no deadlock if someone outside calls .Result.
cards/1/task: The code with .Result hangs. Fix it inside the library without touching the handler.
cards/2/options/0: A pool thread ran the continuation, and the task completed without the UI thread
cards/2/explain: The UI thread was still stuck on .Result, but the task no longer needed it.
cards/3/task: Now the method updates a window control after await. What happens with ConfigureAwait(false)?
cards/4/options/0: After ConfigureAwait(false) the code ran on a pool thread, and controls may only be touched from the UI thread
cards/4/explain: ConfigureAwait(false) belongs only where the code after await doesn't need the UI thread.
cards/5/body:
In libraries, use ConfigureAwait(false) on every await. In app code that touches the UI, leave it out.

But ConfigureAwait is a safety net, not a cure. The real cure for deadlock is not blocking at all: that's the next lesson.
cards/5/deep: .NET 8 added ConfigureAwaitOptions: for example, await task.ConfigureAwait(ConfigureAwaitOptions.SuppressThrowing) waits for the task without throwing. ASP.NET Core has no context, so ConfigureAwait(false) in app code changes nothing there.
cards/6/q: Where does ConfigureAwait(false) belong? Select all that apply.
cards/6/options/2: In a button handler that then updates label.Text
cards/6/options/3: In a Unity script that then moves a transform
cards/6/explain: Where the code after await touches the UI or the Unity API, you need the context.
cards/7/q: ConfigureAwait(false) is on the method's first await but not the second. What's the risk?
cards/7/options/0: If the first task completed at once, the context never changed, and the second await captures the UI context again
cards/7/explain: An await that completes synchronously doesn't switch threads. That's why libraries put ConfigureAwait(false) on every await.
